title.narrative: Togo's Second Sustainable and Inclusive Development Policy Financing

description.narrative: Support green, inclusive and resilient development in Togo by (i) promoting sustainable agriculture, rural electrification and climate action; (ii) boosting human capital and the resilience of vulnerable populations, and (iii) rebuilding fiscal space for priority interventions.

This Second Sustainable and Inclusive Development Policy Financing is the second in a series of two operations to support the foundation for Green, Resilient and Inclusive Development (GRID) in Togo. The Program Development Objectives (PDO) are to (i) promote sustainable agriculture, rural electrification, and climate action; (ii) boost human capital and the resilience of vulnerable populations; and (iii) rebuild fiscal space for priority interventions. The operation will help address Togo's key development challenges in ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity on a livable planet identified in recent World Bank diagnostics1 by boosting economic opportunities in rural areas in an equitable and climate-conscious way, strengthening the resilience of vulnerable populations, improving learning outcomes in underserved areas, empowering women and supporting macroeconomic stability. It will also help leverage the private sector to meet development needs, focusing on attracting new investments in the agriculture and energy sector. The proposed operation includes an International Development Association (IDA) credit of EUR 178.8 million (US200 million dollars equivalent) provided on standard 50-year IDA credit terms.

title.narrative: Number of Flagship safety net beneficiary households with a female designated beneficiary

comment.narrative: On track (close to the target at about 80 percent). The team is following up on recent reforms, including the adoption of the National Social Protection Policy in December 2025 and the revised National Non-Contributory Social Protection Program in March 2026. These reforms are expected to support a relaunch of safety net programs in 2026, including through the ASTRE Program-for-Results (PforR), whose restructuring is nearing completion to align with the government's updated vision for the social protection sector.

title.narrative: Share of households registered in the social registry of individuals and households (RSPM)

comment.narrative: Not achieved at the operation's closing date, but partial achievement is expected by end-2026. Deployment of RSPM is expected to start in Q2 of calendar year 2026. Delays are explained by delays on rollout of e-ID amid fiscal consolidation efforts– PIP resources in 2024 were insufficient to start mass registration, which delayed e-ID rollout by 9 months. Unique identification number of at least one hh member is required to be able to register in RSPM. To date, the government has adopted a decree defining vulnerability criteria, validated the RSPM application methodology and data collection questionnaire, and established the IT architecture, with data collection scheduled to begin in May 2026.

Not achieved at the operation's closing date, but partial achievement is expected by end-2026. The issuance of the first Livret Foncier was put on hold after the U.S. administration suspended MCA funding in January 2025, reducing LRAP's capacity to support the pilot Livret Foncier initiative. Following the discontinuation of MCA support, the Government has mobilized domestic financial resources and authorized the establishment of a Project Management Unit (PMU) to take over land-related activities previously supported by the MCA. The PMU has been given a preliminary mandate to issue the first round of Livrets Fonciers by end-2026.

title.narrative: Tax expenditures in percentage of overall revenues

comment.narrative: Not achieved at the operation's closing date, but partial achievement is expected by end-2026. Due to an increase in the number of tax exemptions. The team assesses that institutional strengthening is required to enable the UPF to play a stronger role in assessing tax exemptions and to improve coordination among entities involved in tax expenditure management. In this context, the team has initiated discussions with the Togolese Revenue Authority (OTR) and the UPF to support the rationalization of tax expenditures, including through a diagnostic review of selected conventions and associated incentives, with a view to containing the growth of tax expenditures over 2026–27.
